children: ) today released Week 7 of its Better 2.0 weekly scorecard, a public record of the company’s turnaround published every Tuesday. This week, Better signed an agreement with a mortgage servicer to offer HELOCs and home equity loans to its existing borrowers, adding a new lead channel with lower customer acquisition costs, and continued to grow partnership volume for its AI-powered HELOC. Better also continued to execute on its cost reduction plan, increasing total realized savings to $0.77 million, well on its path towards its $64.2 million target.

Since the Week 6 scorecard published on November 17, Better has realized additional efficiencies in its corporate organization, expected to generate $38.97 million in annualized savings. Better intends to action an additional $1.5 million in vendor related reductions by December 1, 2026.

“HELOC volume with our partner continues to grow each week, four more brokerages are lined up to join our wholesale platform, and two new partnerships are set to launch. At the same time, we're moving toward a signed agreement to sell Birmingham Bank, which will let us focus fully on our US business,” said Vishal Garg, Founder and Head of Product, Platform and Innovation at Better.
Additional efficiencies in mortgage operations expected to deliver $770K in annualized savings
Actioning additional $1.5M in vendor related reductions
Finish executing efficiency initiatives to complete total identified savings in Week 6 scorecard
Pushing identified efficiencies through every function to close the gap to the $64.2M target
Better's AI-powered HELOC with large existing customer live; partnership volume scaling weekly
Signed agreement with mortgage servicers to offer HELOCs and home equity loans to existing borrowers, opening a new lead channel with lower customer acquisition costs
Building multichannel campaign to scale to Better Wholesale and continue onboarding new brokerages
Four additional mortgage brokerages in the pipeline to be onboarded onto Better’s wholesale platform
Previously announced long-term partnerships with rental credit management platform and home inspection company aiming to launch early next week
Making progress with 3 other major partners and one new revived large-scale partnership
Continue progressing the planned sale of Birmingham Bank, Better's UK bank subsidiary

Continue advancing discussions with prospective financing partners following receipt of five term sheets for approximately $50 million in debt financing tied to the planned sale of Birmingham Bank, Better’s UK bank subsidiary
Better will continue to publish its management scorecard weekly until it achieves Adjusted EBITDA breakeven, reporting completed actions, outstanding commitments and changes to timelines.

) is the first AI-native mortgage and home equity finance platform, and first fintech to fund more than $115 billion in loan volume. Since 2016, Better has leveraged its industry-leading AI platform, Tinman®, to achieve a singular mission of making homeownership cheaper, faster, and easier for all Americans. Tinman® allows customers to see their rate options in seconds, get pre-approved in minutes, lock in rates, and close their loan in as little as three weeks. In addition, Betsy®, leveraging Tinman® MCP, the first AI loan agent built exclusively for the mortgage industry, is revolutionizing the homebuying journey by delivering timely application status updates to consumers, answering questions, and moving their loan application along 24/7/365. Better’s mortgage offerings include GSE-conforming, FHA, VA loans, jumbo, and Non-QM mortgage loans as well as home equity loans. Better serves customers in all 50 US states.
For more information, follow @tinmanAI on X and @betterdotcom on Instagram and TikTok.
